business_summary.text: Godavari Biorefineries operates an integrated biorefinery model converting agricultural feedstocks into food (sugar), fuel (ethanol), and chemicals (bio-based specialty chemicals). The company is also developing drug candidates including a triple-negative breast cancer molecule.

call_points.text: Bio-based chemicals revenue guided at ₹190 Cr for Q2FY27, growing to ₹240 Cr quarterly after debottlenecking
₹25 Cr investment in bio-based chemicals debottlenecking to increase capacity utilization
Strong customer interest in bio-based chemicals due to fossil price volatility and supply chain concerns
Bio-based chemicals EBITDA margin expanded to 11.4% from 8.9% YoY, with further improvement expected
Debt levels expected to remain stable with focus on maintaining current debt-equity structure
200 KLPD grain distillery adds about 60 million litres a year; most equipment on site, commissioning trials targeted next month.
Bio-based chemical demand seen stronger this financial year from this quarter, helped by debottlenecking done last year.
Margin pressure in FY26 came from higher cane prices without an increase in sugar MSP or ethanol blend price.
Ethanol sold about 98 million litres in FY26 across EBP, ENA and other grades; EBP remains the main outlet.
Ethyl acetate output is raised opportunistically when ethanol is long and its margin is better, alongside the specialty strategy.
Ethanol price revision is the government's call; industry has asked for a rise after three years of higher cane prices.
West Asia crisis raised freight and raw material costs and disrupted supply for some chemicals in Q4.
DME pilot plant research needs another 3 to 6 months before commercialisation questions can be answered.
Grain distillery economics deferred until government announces ethanol prices around September-October 2026.

operating_notes.text: FY26 exceptional charge of ₹31.14 Cr comprises ₹4.48 Cr for New Labour Codes and ₹26.66 Cr for additional 2023-24 harvest charges.
Sugar segment FY26 operating profit was ₹49.69 Cr against ₹25.90 Cr in FY25; distillery fell to ₹9.47 Cr from ₹14.94 Cr.
Foreign subsidiaries contributed ₹58.81 Cr revenue and ₹1.35 Cr net profit before consolidation adjustments in FY26.
Achieved highest-ever cane crushing of 2.5 Mn tonnes in 2025-26 season.
FY26 ethanol equivalent sales about 98 million litres across EBP, ENA and other grades.
Ethanol net realisation: B-heavy molasses about 60-plus, juice to ethanol about 65-plus, maize to ethanol around 72.
Energy mix about 85% bagasse and 15% coal; highest-ever cane crushing of 2.5 million tonnes in 2025-26 season.
Sugar inventory at quarter end: 65,000 tons
DME pilot trials expected to conclude latest by March 2027
Bio-butanol MoU secured with Synthomer for chemical intermediate use

timeline.summary: Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹564.1 Cr (-2.7% YoY), net profit ₹52.88 Cr (-26.5% YoY).
Godavari Biorefineries reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹564.1 Cr and net profit of ₹52.9 Cr.
Manoj Jain, Director, signed the audio recording of Q4 and FY26 earnings conference call uploaded on May 26, 2026.
On May 27, 2026, Godavari Biorefineries received a 20-year patent from the Indian Patent Office for its process for production of branched alcohol.

Godavari Biorefineries' Q4/FY26 call (May 26, 2026): FY26 total income ₹2,000.2 Cr (+6%), EBITDA ₹139.3 Cr (+15.8%), PAT ₹3.5 Cr; 200 KLPD grain distillery commissioning trials targeted for June 2026.

Godavari Biorefineries held Q1FY27 earnings call on 7 August 2026, reporting revenue of ₹557.9 Cr (+4.6% YoY) and net loss of ₹19.3 Cr, with strong bio-based chemicals growth and plans for capacity expansion
Godavari Biorefineries received a US patent grant for a novel cancer treatment compound on October 14, 2026.
